title: Chapter 48 — The Trade Desk: Setting Up Your B2B Operation
intro: The operational architecture — running trade inside a retail floor with systems and boundaries.

sections.title: Trade Inside Retail
sections.content:
Most appliance retailers run their trade business inside their retail operation. This creates tension — trade customers expect dedicated attention, fast quotes, and priority delivery, while retail customers walk in expecting the same.

The trade desk is not a physical desk — it is a system. It includes dedicated quote templates, trade pricing tiers, delivery prioritization, a CRM pipeline separate from retail, and a rep who owns the trade relationships.

sections.title: Setting Boundaries
sections.content:
Trade customers should have a direct line to their rep — phone, text, email. They should not have to walk in and wait behind retail customers for a quote.

Quote turnaround: same day, ideally within hours. Delivery scheduling: priority windows. Pricing: pre-negotiated tiers based on volume commitment. Payment: net terms for established accounts.

These boundaries protect both the trade relationship and the retail floor. Without them, trade customers get frustrated by retail pace and retail customers get neglected while the rep handles trade calls.

sections.title: The Account Review Rhythm
sections.content:
Every trade account should have a quarterly review. Pull the numbers: total revenue, number of projects, average ticket, delivery issues, open quotes. Compare to the same quarter last year.

The review meeting is where you identify growth opportunities, address problems, and strengthen the relationship. 'Your volume is up 15 percent this quarter. I want to make sure our pricing still works for you. And I noticed two delivery issues — let me walk you through what we changed to prevent those.'
